Odin × Godot

odin_godot documentation website

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Publish from the SDK repository with GitHub PagesScrapyard showcase

The SDK home page, task-based documentation, API notes, examples, and illustrated multiplayer guide. The site uses a shared o/g header, documentation sidebar, on-page navigation, and keyboard-accessible search.

Open the home page, or serve it from this repository root:

Shell
python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory docs/visual-guide/dist

Visit http://127.0.0.1:8765. There is no installation or build step. Serving over HTTP enables documentation search and legacy reference redirects. Use Print / save PDF on an article for a paper copy.

The main entry points are SDK docs, examples, the multiplayer field guide, and the complete library. Existing article URLs remain valid.

The desk reference, print edition, and six SVG diagrams are standalone artifacts. dist/ is the complete portable website. The PDF captures the article in its initial state; the website retains the interactive controls.

The home page is generated by build-product.mjs. site-structure.mjs defines routes and documentation navigation. dist/sdk.css and dist/site.js supply the shared layout and search. The visual field guide remains authored in dist/guide.html; dist/app.js drives its interactive models.

Task-based tutorials live in content/. build-readers.mjs renders them and the repository's linked documents into HTML, with highlighted code, tables, and static diagrams. Related Markdown links resolve to other reading pages. Original source files remain available as downloads.

Viewing the site needs no dependencies. To regenerate the reading pages, SVGs, and source snapshots after API changes, install the pinned build dependencies once:

Shell
cd docs/visual-guide
npm ci

Then, from the repository root:

Shell
node docs/visual-guide/prepare.mjs

build-readers.mjs follows links from the guide's selected references and generates the supplemental reading library. New Mermaid diagrams are rendered to static SVG using Chrome; set GUIDE_CHROME if Chrome is installed at a nonstandard path. Cached SVGs do not require a browser. Newly rendered diagrams are serialized as XML and decoded as images before publication. The link checker also rejects malformed SVGs and unresolved escape tokens. No Markdown parser or diagram runtime ships to visitors.

The generator reads repository files, records their Git baseline in dist/reference-manifest.json, and refreshes the bundled copies. It does not change the original docs, frameworks, or game examples. The browser correction model is deliberately smaller than the Odin Loot model; it is not a runtime port.

The hosting manifest in .openai/hosting.json identifies the private Sites publication. The website needs no connected apps, credentials, or backend.

Publish from the SDK repository with GitHub Pages#

Keep this guide in odin_godot. GitHub calls this a project site, with the default address https://wlitwin.github.io/odin_godot/. A user site at wlitwin.github.io would instead need a repository named wlitwin.github.io. The project site keeps documentation changes with the SDK versions they describe.

The Documentation workflow installs the pinned documentation tools, regenerates the guide and reading pages, checks local links and section anchors, and publishes only docs/visual-guide/dist. Pull requests build and check the site; pushes to main deploy it independently of the game tests. No GitHub token or hosting secret needs to be added.

One-time setup after committing and pushing these files:

  1. Open Settings → Pages.
  2. Under Build and deployment, choose GitHub Actions as the source.
  3. Run Documentation from the Actions tab, or push the next change to main.
  4. After the deployment succeeds, use https://wlitwin.github.io/odin_godot/ for the repository's website field and documentation link.

All assets, reading links, and JavaScript fetches use relative paths, so the same output works at a project subpath, a user-site root, or a custom domain. The Pages artifact is the contents of dist, with its index.html at the artifact root; it does not need Jekyll or a gh-pages branch.

Check an updated build locally with:

Shell
node docs/visual-guide/prepare.mjs
python3 docs/visual-guide/check-site.py

GitHub's instructions: project and user sites and publishing through Actions.

Scrapyard showcase#

The home page links to the live Scrapyard browser build and uses a screenshot captured from that build. It also links to the repository's Replay Scrapyard contributor and code guides. The live build and the Replay port have separate implementation histories; the showcase does not assign a framework or parity claim to an unversioned itch.io upload.
